# Shepherd of Hermas Chapter 61 — The EMET Bible (Literal)

**Translator:** EMET | **Source:** P.Mich. 130, Shepherd of Hermas 61 | **Source Image:** source-texts/greek-EC/SHE_061_page_001.jpg

---

## Similitude 5, Part 7 — Do Not Grieve the Holy Spirit in Your Flesh

**61:1** "I should like, lord," I said, "to know whether, in the case of those who have died before the days of these repentances, there is any hope for them." "Come," he said, "and I will show you concerning all those who have doubted and have sinned."

**61:2** He showed me a young man sitting on a chair and speaking to many men. "Do you see the young man?" "Yes, lord," I said. "This is the angel of righteousness," he said. "And there are standing around him many men of various kinds. Some are being brought before him, and some are going away with joy, and some are going away in grief."

**61:3** "And many," he said, "are standing around and listening. Some who stand up to go away are joyful; others grieve and weep. Lord, I do not understand what all this means." "Listen," he said. "The young man you see sitting on the chair is the angel of righteousness. The men who are brought to him are those who are to receive repentance. Hear also why some go away joyful and others sorrowful."

**61:4** "Those who go away joyful are those who have taken these words into their hearts and have repented with all their heart. To them repentance is given. But those who go away sorrowful are those who have completely turned away from God and do not repent. For to these, repentance of life is not given."

**61:5** "But what about those who doubted?" "And what about those," I said, "who have only sinned and not repented?" "To those who have doubted," he said, "repentance is given according to the state of their heart." He said to me: "Do not let the devil find an entrance into your heart. He is crafty and cunning, turning aside the servants of God; especially those who are double-minded. So be strong in your faith and do not waver."

---

*EMET renders the Greek of P.Mich. 130 with maximal literalness, preserving the angel-of-righteousness vision and the doctrine of repentance in Similitude 5.*
